findings.message: `compose_pipeline` is keyword-only and currently builds its own registry via `stages.compose` (`squatch/stages.py:1126`, `Registry(config)`). The criteria say every construction site must receive the one shared payload, and the Definition of rejected forbids a second registry payload. That means the payload has to become a required parameter; a default that falls back to `Registry(config)` would be exactly the forbidden dual path. Five existing direct callers outside the fence would then break: `eval/shakeout/bench.py:82`, `eval/daemon_soak.py:387`, `tests/test_merge.py:92,739`, `tests/test_mergequeue.py:717,780,939,1000`, `tests/test_daemon_composition.py:342`.
findings.paved_road: fix the plan, then re-author the ticket

findings.message: `Serve.compose` builds its own `Registry(config)`, and `restart_session`/`Session` must now carry the Timers/payload instance. `tests/test_serve.py` and `eval/daemon_soak.py` drive `Serve`, and `tests/test_restart_timers.py` constructs `Session(journal, None)` directly. Of these, only `tests/test_restart_timers.py` is fenced. Because the plan's core fence is fixed ('sole Phase 4 ... core-fence authority; later tails may refine then-existing Context'), the author cannot add the missing callers.
